comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT. GitHub #645's design (mitcad#2494; opened with --open, never committed; tools/cli/shell-sharp-reported-test.cmake) with its top rounding suppressed, as the reporter tried it on 25.11.2026: Body1 (F6.b0), a loft (Loft1 F6) cut to a slot with round ends (Extrude1 F9), its top F6:side(c2)#1 a face of the loft's periodic surface. Shell with the top removed, Inside 1, 2 and 3 mm. A Shell that builds passes MitCad's validity check (an invalid result is an error of the feature).
Sharp, 1 mm: it built before too (9576.682 mm3, 11 faces: the body's five kept faces, their offsets and the top's rim).

Rounded, 1 mm: it failed ('the offset faces do not close up'). The offset of the slot's near round end, extended to the top in the arc join, meets the top's periodic surface in a section split into three pieces (at the seam of the extended round end, at the end of the extended face and where the section's curve was computed in two); one piece was kept, it stopped short of the plane beside, and the round end's offset got no wire. Now the run of pieces is glued into one edge (OCCT port patch 2494). The body has no concave edge, so the arc join gives the wall the intersection join gives: the same volume.
2 mm, Sharp (it built before too) and Rounded (it failed as at 1 mm).
3 mm, Sharp (it built before too) and Rounded (it failed as at 1 mm).
